subject: ela
intro: Strong readers of nonfiction do two jobs. First, they find the exact words that a text says out loud. That is an explicit detail. Second, they add clues together to figure out something the author hints at but does not say directly. That is an inference. Either way, you must point back to the text. When you answer, name the sentence or example that proves it. Saying "The text says..." is how you show your evidence.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Honeybees live in large groups called colonies. A single colony can hold more than 50,000 bees. Each bee has a job. Worker bees gather nectar, nurse bees feed the young, and one queen lays all of the eggs.

Who lays the eggs in a honeybee colony? Answer using a detail from the text.

steps: The question asks for an explicit detail, so I look for the exact words.
The text says, "one queen lays all of the eggs."
That sentence states the answer directly, so I quote it as my evidence.
solution.answer: The queen lays the eggs. The text says, "one queen lays all of the eggs."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

When a desert night falls, the sand cools quickly. The kangaroo rat leaves its burrow only after dark. It never drinks water. Instead, its body makes water from the dry seeds it eats.

Using details from the text, explain why the kangaroo rat can survive without ever drinking water.

steps: I look for the sentence that explains how the animal gets water.
The text says, "its body makes water from the dry seeds it eats."
That detail explains how it survives without drinking, so I use it as evidence.
solution.answer: The kangaroo rat survives because its body makes its own water. The text says, "its body makes water from the dry seeds it eats."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Jane Goodall traveled to Africa in 1960 to study wild chimpanzees. At first the chimps ran from her. She sat quietly in the same spot for months. Slowly, the chimps stopped fearing her and let her come close.

Why did the chimps stop running from Jane Goodall? Draw an inference and support it with a detail.

steps: The text does not say the reason in one sentence, so I must infer it.
It says she "sat quietly in the same spot for months" and that the chimps "slowly" stopped fearing her.
Putting these clues together, her patience made the chimps feel safe.
solution.answer: I can infer that the chimps stopped running because Jane was patient and calm. The text says she "sat quietly in the same spot for months," which made the chimps feel safe over time.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A lighthouse stands at the edge of the rocky shore. Its bright light spins in a slow circle all night long. Long ago, ships crashed on these rocks in the dark. Since the lighthouse was built, no ship has wrecked here.

What can you infer is the purpose of the lighthouse? Use a detail to support your answer.

steps: The purpose is not stated directly, so I gather clues.
The text says ships once "crashed on these rocks in the dark" but "no ship has wrecked here" since it was built.
This tells me the light helps ships avoid the rocks at night.
solution.answer: I can infer the lighthouse warns ships away from the rocks so they do not crash. The text says that since it was built, "no ship has wrecked here."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The Sahara is the largest hot desert on Earth. It covers most of northern Africa. During the day, the temperature can rise above 100 degrees. Very little rain falls there, sometimes none for years.

What is the largest hot desert on Earth? Answer with a detail from the text.

steps: The question asks for an explicit fact.
The text says, "The Sahara is the largest hot desert on Earth."
I quote that sentence as my evidence.
solution.answer: The Sahara is the largest hot desert on Earth. The text states this directly in the first sentence.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Thomas Edison tried thousands of materials before he found one that worked in his light bulb. Each time a material burned out too fast, he wrote down what he had learned and tried again. He said he had not failed, he had simply found ways that did not work.

Using details from the text, explain what kind of worker Edison was.

steps: The text does not use one word to describe him, so I infer his traits from his actions.
It says he "tried thousands of materials" and after each failure "tried again."
These details show he did not give up easily.
solution.answer: I can infer that Edison was determined and did not give up. The text says he "tried thousands of materials" and after each one burned out he "tried again."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Sea otters float on their backs while they eat. To keep from drifting apart while they sleep, a group of otters will hold paws. Sometimes they even wrap themselves in kelp so the waves cannot carry them away.

Why do sea otters hold paws while sleeping? Answer with a detail from the text.

steps: The question asks for a stated reason.
The text says they hold paws so they do not "drift apart while they sleep."
I use that detail as my evidence.
solution.answer: Sea otters hold paws so they will not drift apart while sleeping. The text says they do this "to keep from drifting apart while they sleep."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Only 14 countries sent athletes, and all of them were men. Today, thousands of athletes from more than 200 countries compete, and women take part in nearly every sport.

What can you infer about how the Olympics have changed? Support your answer with details.

steps: I compare the details about 1896 with the details about today.
In 1896 only 14 countries and only men competed, but today more than 200 countries and women take part.
Comparing these shows the Games grew much larger and more open.
solution.answer: I can infer the Olympics have grown much bigger and more open to everyone. The text says only 14 countries and only men joined in 1896, but today more than 200 countries and women compete.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Monarch butterflies cannot survive cold winters in the north. Each fall, millions of them fly south to warmer forests in Mexico. The trip is over 2,000 miles long. Amazingly, these butterflies have never made the trip before, yet they find the exact same forests their great-grandparents used.

Why do monarch butterflies fly south each fall? Answer with a detail, then explain one thing that is surprising about their trip.

steps: First I find the stated reason for the trip.
The text says monarchs "cannot survive cold winters in the north," so they fly to "warmer forests."
Then I find the surprising detail: they find the same forests even though they "have never made the trip before."
solution.answer: Monarchs fly south because they "cannot survive cold winters in the north," so they seek warmer forests. What is surprising is that they "find the exact same forests their great-grandparents used" even though they have never made the trip before.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Inside a beaver's dam sits a cozy den called a lodge. The only doors are underwater, so no wolf or bear can walk in. Beavers store branches under the ice nearby. When snow covers the pond, they still have food and a warm, dry home.

Ask one question that a detail answers directly, and one question that needs an inference. Then answer both using the text.

steps: For the direct question, I pick a fact stated in the text.
For the inference question, I pick something the text hints at.
I answer each one using evidence from the passage.
solution.answer: Direct question: Where are the doors to the lodge? Answer: underwater, because the text says, "The only doors are underwater." Inference question: Why are the doors underwater? Answer: to keep out predators, because the text says "no wolf or bear can walk in."
